## The puzzle

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

China's air-defense-identification-zone incursions into Taiwan's ADIZ dropped from 3,764 in 2025 to 147 in February 2026 — the lowest of the Lai era. Western analysts read this two ways: as Chinese retreat under Trump's preventive-force demonstration, or as patient signaling. Beijing simultaneously moved on Scarborough Shoal, ran PLA Eastern Theater transits, escalated CIPS volume, and lobbied for a Trump-Xi summit. The same evidence supports opposite readings. Which one is right depends on what game China is playing.

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

China's air-defense-identification-zone (ADIZ) incursions into Taiwan's ADIZ — a major proxy for cross-strait coercive pressure — dropped from 3,764 in 2025 (the high-water mark of the Lai era) to **147 in February 2026**, the lowest monthly total since Lai's inauguration. April rebounded modestly to 169. Western analysts read this two ways. The retreat reading: Trump demonstrated preventive force in Iran (28 February 2026 strikes after Israeli pre-strike); Xi updated upward on US-resolve and pulled back. The patience reading: China is conserving signaling capacity while pursuing Trump-Xi summit-mediated bargaining (announced May 14-15) and structural financial-architecture wins (CIPS daily volume ~$134B; MOFCOM May 2 blocking statute on five teapot refineries handling ~25% of Chinese refining capacity). The same evidence supports opposite readings. Meanwhile Beijing moved on Scarborough Shoal (4 March; 352m floating barrier installed 11 April), ran a PLA Eastern Theater Joint Combat Group transit 19-22 April, sailed the Liaoning carrier 20 April, ran Type 076 and Type 055 trials, and intensified diplomatic engagement with Iran (Wang-Araghchi 6 May). The puzzle Q8 sets: what is China actually doing, and what does the 2026 Iran war mean for Taiwan?

## Methodology — why unitary Friedberg-dominant beats dimension-specific

This chapter applies the standard 8-step protocol. The devil's-advocate pass forced the most consequential revision: the F1-F6 framework structure originally posited (financial, intentions, operational, etc.) was analyst-constructed, not literature-derived. Friedberg's framework explicitly integrates economic statecraft + strategic patience + asymmetric leverage + capability build as components of one strategy. META rule 7 (literature-derived domain-distinction required for principled-multi-framework finding) was rejected for Q8; headline reverted to unitary Friedberg with Brands-Beckley peaking-power patience overlay. Posterior on the unitary headline is capped at 0.40 by the T3-inference inventory (five load-bearing T3 inferences). Five summit-specific tests are pre-registered for the May 14-15 Trump-Xi meeting; five 6-month structural tests are pre-registered through end-Q3 2026.
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-stage1"}
[**Two readings of the same data.** The ADIZ tempo drop from 3,764 (2025) to 147 (Feb 2026) is real. Reading 1: China is retreating — Trump's Iran preventive-force demonstration updates Xi upward on US-resolve; the pullback follows. Reading 2: China is patient — conserving signaling capacity while pursuing Trump-Xi summit deliverables and structural financial-architecture wins. The readings make different predictions about post-summit Chinese behavior.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**Two readings of the same observed pattern.** The empirical fact: Taiwan MOD recorded 3,764 PLA ADIZ incursions in calendar 2025 (the high-water mark of Lai's first year), 147 in February 2026 (the lowest monthly total since Lai's inauguration), and 169 in April (a modest rebound). The same observation supports opposite readings. *Reading 1 — retreat under updated US-resolve:* Trump's 28 February 2026 preventive strikes on Iran (after Israel's 27 February preemption) demonstrate willingness to use force preventively. Xi observes; updates upward on US resolve; pulls back from ADIZ pressure. This is Slantchev-style information-revelation-through-action plus Hudson Lee's resolve-demonstration channel; it predicts Chinese pullback compounds if Trump's preventive-force pattern persists. *Reading 2 — patient signaling optimizing for summit bargaining:* China is conserving signaling capacity for a different purpose. With the Trump-Xi summit announced for May 14-15 (Beijing, focus on trade + Taiwan arms sales + Iran-war relief), China extracts non-kinetic wins through diplomatic channels rather than burning leverage on coercive air patrols. Meanwhile structural financial-architecture wins compound: PRC MOFCOM blocking statute of 2 May 2026 over Hengli plus four other teapot refineries (covering ~25% of Chinese refining capacity) is the first formal Chinese legal defiance of US secondary sanctions; CIPS daily volume reaches ~$134B in March 2026. The two readings predict different post-summit behavior — retreat predicts continued ADIZ suppression regardless of summit outcome; patience predicts ADIZ-tempo recovery if summit delivers no Taiwan-related concessions.
:::

::: {focus-on="cr-stage2"}
[**Four mechanisms, one strategy.** σ structural financial-architecture (CIPS + blocking statute, persists regardless of summit); ε summit-mediated Taiwan concessions (heavily conditional on May 14-15 outcome); ι PLA development continuing but operationally bounded by Zhang Youxia / 73rd Group Army purges; τ bounded asymmetric intentions-update per [Yarhi-Milo]{.gloss data-gloss="yarhi-milo-selective-attention"}. The four collapse into one [Friedberg]{.gloss data-gloss="friedberg-win-without-fighting"} strategy rather than four independent findings.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**The four mechanisms.** *σ — Structural financial-architecture maturation.* PRC MOFCOM 2 May 2026 blocking statute over Hengli plus four other teapot refineries — the first formal Chinese legal defiance of US secondary sanctions — combined with CIPS daily volume at ~$134B and Hengli's 235B yuan bank credit facility (despite verbal Chinese-bank loan suspensions) constitutes structural lock-in. This is Eichengreen's "gradual shift toward a multi-currency system" rather than a sudden rupture, but the directionality is unambiguous, and the architecture persists regardless of summit outcome. P(load-bearing) ≈ 0.60. *ε — Summit-mediated Taiwan-related US concessions.* The Trump-Xi summit (Beijing, 14-15 May 2026) pairs trade (~$14B in pending Taiwan arms sales as bargaining chip), Taiwan (declaratory-shift options), and Iran-war relief. The pre-summit analyst consensus (CSIS Kagan; Brookings Hass-Czin; CFR Froman/Doshi-Sacks; Bruegel García-Herrero) is "modest substance, ambitious optics." Specific Taiwan-rhetoric shifts Taipei is bracing against: "not supporting" Taiwan independence → "opposing"; "support" for "peaceful unification"; arms-sale self-restraint; "one China principle" rather than "policy." P(load-bearing) ≈ 0.45 — heavily conditioned on summit outcome (4 days out). *ι — PLA capability execution bounds.* Naval News 5 May 2026 documents Type 076 *Sichuan* sea trials, Type 055 *Zunyi* live-fire during Balikatan-2026, Liaoning carrier 20 April transit, H-6/YJ-12 patrols. Platform development continues. But [Biddle's modern-system theory]{.gloss data-gloss="biddle-modern-system"} requires functioning command structures + sustained doctrine + training cycles for combined-arms execution; the Zhang Youxia / Liu Zhenli / 73rd Group Army purges (Jamestown) bound execution through 2027-28. P(load-bearing) ≈ 0.55. *τ — Bounded asymmetric intentions-update.* Xi observes Trump's Iran preventive-force willingness; the question is what Xi updates *on*. Xi updates substantially upward on US-Iran-resolve (Hudson Lee resolve-demonstration channel). But [Yarhi-Milo's selective-attention framework]{.gloss data-gloss="yarhi-milo-selective-attention"} predicts the update on US-Taiwan-resolve is *bounded* — Xi is anchored on Taiwan-specific priors (different theater, different historical pattern). And Weisiger interest-channel transmission cuts the other way: observing US prioritization of Iran can be read as US deprioritization of Taiwan. Net effect: Xi's update on US-Taiwan-defense-resolve is modest and ambiguous. P(load-bearing) ≈ 0.45.
:::
:::

::: {.deep-only}
**Five pre-registered summit tests.** Each test is a specific outcome that, if observed, updates the posterior on the Friedberg-dominant finding. *Test 1 — Taiwan declaratory shift:* does the summit produce a US declaratory shift from "not supporting" to "opposing" Taiwan independence in joint statements or readouts? *Test 2 — Arms-sale self-restraint:* does the US announce any pause, delay, or reduction in the $14B Taiwan arms package? *Test 3 — "One China principle" vs "policy":* does the US shift from "one China policy" (the standard US phrasing since 1979) to "one China principle" (the PRC phrasing implying acceptance of Beijing's sovereignty claim)? *Test 4 — Iran-Hormuz mediation language:* does the summit produce explicit Chinese-mediation language on Iran-war wind-down + Hormuz reopening? *Test 5 — CRINK secondary-sanctions concession:* does the summit produce explicit US concessions on secondary sanctions affecting CRINK financial architecture (Hengli, teapot refineries)? *Aggregate revision rule:* count how many tests fire "yes." 4-5 yes → P(Friedberg-dominant) → 0.60. 2-3 yes → P → 0.45 (current). 0-1 yes → P → 0.25; Steel-man B unitary (China net loser on Taiwan-relevant dimensions) rises to 0.45. The pre-registration makes the synthesis testable within four days.

::: {focus-on="cr-stage4"}
[**Five 6-month structural tests.** CIPS scaling validates σ as structural-breakpoint rather than gradual shift; blocking statute extension validates structural-defiance; PLA combined-arms recovery would falsify the ι 2027-28 bound; Chinese strategic-discourse incorporation tests whether Western Position 2+3 framings reflect Chinese learning; τ disambiguation tests whether Xi reads Iran preventive force as Taiwan-relevant resolve signal.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**Five 6-month structural tests.** *Test 6 — CIPS scaling:* does CIPS daily volume reach $200B sustained by end-Q3 2026? If yes, σ validates as structural-breakpoint; if no, Eichengreen's gradual-shift framing validates. *Test 7 — Blocking statute extension:* does the May 2 blocking statute extend to additional Chinese firms (Sinopec/CNPC/CNOOC subsidiaries) or to non-Iran sanctions targets (Russia-buyer intermediaries)? Extension would very strongly validate σ; non-extension would keep the May 2 datum as symbolic-defensive. *Test 8 — PLA combined-arms recovery:* does the PLA show evidence of combined-arms exercises beyond platform demonstrations — cross-service integration, command-recovery from purges? If yes, ι constraint partially falsifies and 2027 readiness becomes plausible. *Test 9 — Chinese strategic-discourse incorporation:* does Chinese strategic discourse (PLA Daily, Global Times, CCP-aligned analysts) incorporate Position 2+3 Hormuz-template framings (law-enforcement-coded or financial-architecture/insurance-blockade approaches)? If yes, Chinese strategic learning validated. If no, the Western-analyst Position 2+3 dominance is framework drift, not Chinese doctrine evolution. *Test 10 — τ disambiguation:* does Chinese strategic discourse show upward update on US-Taiwan-defense-resolve specifically (not US-resolve generally)? If yes, Yarhi-Milo selective-attention bound partially falsifies. The five 6-month tests, combined with the five 4-day summit tests, give the analysis ten distinct empirical hooks.
:::

### Figure 4 — Source-confidence tier audit

Of the synthesis's load-bearing claims:

- **[T1]{.tier .tier-1} multi-source verified:** Taiwan ADIZ tempo (3,764 in 2025; 147 in Feb 2026; 169 in April) — Taiwan MOD + USCC China Bulletin; Scarborough Shoal 4 March + floating barrier 11 April — USCC + CSMonitor; PRC MOFCOM 2 May blocking statute over 5 teapot refineries (~25% of Chinese refining capacity) — Bloomberg + Al Jazeera; Wang-Araghchi 6 May — PRC MOFA; Trump-Xi summit 14-15 May (Iran + Taiwan + arms-sale central) — multiple primary sources; Taiwan NT$780B special defense budget — Taipei Times + Taiwan MOD.

- **[T2]{.tier .tier-2} single-source named:** PLA Eastern Theater 19-22 April transit + Liaoning + Type 076 trials + Type 055 live-fire — Naval News May 5; CIPS daily volume ~$134B March 2026 — CSIS China Power + Bloomberg; Hengli 235B yuan bank credit + verbally-instructed loan suspensions — AEI May 8; China Gulf imports -25% YoY March 2026 — Brookings; AEI April 17 CRINK satellite intel; PLA purges (Zhang Youxia / Liu Zhenli / 73rd Group Army) — Jamestown; Freymann customs-quarantine framework (FA April 29); CFR May 10 5-author consensus; Bruegel García-Herrero May 8 + SCMP Magnier May 9 same consensus.

- **[T3]{.tier .tier-3} inference from evidence:** **[Brands-Beckley peaking-power patience explains observed pattern]{.gloss data-gloss="brands-beckley-peaking-power"}** (inference); **[Friedberg "win without fighting" is the operative unitary framework]{.gloss data-gloss="friedberg-win-without-fighting"}** (preferred over Allison/Brands-Beckley standalone; the central load-bearing inference); China cannot execute 2027 Taiwan op due to purge effects (inference from Jamestown via [Biddle modern-system theory]{.gloss data-gloss="biddle-modern-system"}); Xi's update on US-Taiwan-resolve is bounded vs US-Iran-resolve update is substantial (inference from [Yarhi-Milo]{.gloss data-gloss="yarhi-milo-selective-attention"} + Weisiger application); Position 2+3 Hormuz-template dominance reflects Western-analyst framework drift, not Chinese strategic learning (DA Critique 7 acknowledgment).

- **[T4]{.tier .tier-4} conjecture:** none in the load-bearing path; "other/hybrid" 15% headline alternative is a tier-4 catch-all.

**Five load-bearing T3 inferences** trigger the META rule 5 posterior cap at ≤ 0.40 on the unitary headline. The reconciled posterior sits exactly at that cap.

## Pre-mortem {#pre-mortem}

The most likely ways the analysis will be wrong:

1. **Trump-Xi summit produces substantial Taiwan-related concessions** (P ≈ 0.20-0.25). The Friedberg-dominant headline validates strongly; posterior should jump to 0.55+.

2. **Trump-Xi summit produces NO Taiwan-related concessions** (P ≈ 0.25-0.30). Steel-man B (China net loser on Taiwan dimensions) reading strengthens; Friedberg-dominant drops to 0.25-0.30.

3. **PLA combined-arms recovery faster than projected** (P ≈ 0.10). ι constraint falsifies; 2027 readiness becomes possible; Brands-Beckley peaking-power acceleration scenario becomes operative.

4. **CIPS scales rapidly beyond gradual-shift framing** (P ≈ 0.15). σ validates as structural-breakpoint; financial-architecture dimension becomes more independent of summit outcome; might force dimension-specific re-reading.

5. **China makes major Taiwan move in 2026-2027** (P ≈ 0.05-0.10). Brands-Beckley acceleration validates; Friedberg patience falsified.

6. **DA Critique 1 was wrong**: the dimension-specific finding might be substantively correct, with Friedberg-unitary being the analyst-convenience over-collapse. P ≈ 0.20.

**Lowest-confidence claim**: that the Western-analyst Position 2+3 Hormuz-template framework drift reflects (or doesn't reflect) actual Chinese strategic-doctrine evolution. The empirical test (Chinese strategic-discourse incorporation) is pre-registered as a 6-month-horizon test, not currently resolvable.
